newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says has enough sugar to meet U.S. quota.
newsitem.headline: Manila says has enough sugar to meet U.S. quota.

text.p: Philippine Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) chief Wilson Gamboa said on Thursday the country has enough locally grown sugar to meet its increased quota to the United States.
The Philippines is a beneficiary of a U.S. sugar import programme to buy the commodity from developing countries at premium prices.

On Tuesday, the U.S. government said it has increased the Philippine sugar quota by 27,411 tonnes for crop year 1996/1997 (Sept-Aug). The original allocation was pegged at 219,000 tonnes at the start of the crop year.
"We have enough sugar for export. In fact, we are in excess because of imports and because we are still at the peak of our milling season," Gamboa told Reuters in a phone interview.
Gamboa said the Philippines has so far already shipped 103,000 tonnes to the United States.
Philippine sugar imports to the United States were pegged at 12 cents per pound against the prevailing 12 to 13 cents per pound in the world market.

Gamboa also said the SRA will conduct public consultations with local sugar producers and millers before it authorises the release of some 100,000 tonnes of unsold sugar in the warehouses of local millers.

The unsold sugar stocks include 27,000 tonnes of refined sugar stacked for 10 months now in the warehouse of the trading arm of Victorias Milling Corp, Gamboa said. Cash-strapped Victorias disclosed debt problems last week.
